title: Ethics in research
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank card covers consent, privacy and withdrawal but has no debriefing or justified-deception content, and its safety focus is built around physical fitness testing, so matching it would need new content rather than small changes.

draft.title: Ethics in research
card: Informed consent means participants are told what will happen and agree to take part. Taking part must be voluntary, with no pressure.
Participants can leave the study at any time. They can also ask for their data to be removed.
Personal details and results are kept private and are not linked to a name without permission.
A debrief at the end explains the true aim and checks the participant is well. Deception is only used when it is justified, and it is then explained in the debrief.
draft.remember: Protect participants: tell them, let them choose and leave, keep their details private, and explain afterwards.

a.q: At the end of a study, a researcher explains its true aim and asks how participants feel. What is this called?
a.why: A debrief happens at the end and explains the true aim and checks wellbeing. Informed consent is tempting, but it happens before the study begins.
a.clue: Think about when it happens: before or after.

b.q: Sam is a student in Ms Lee's class. She tells him his marks will drop if he does not join her study. Which protection is broken?
b.why: Threatening his marks pressures Sam, so taking part is not voluntary. Consent is also affected, but the main problem is the pressure, not a lack of information.
b.clue: Was Sam free to say no?
